findings.reason: without `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` in §3's write paths and the two values carried onto the launched pointer (or onto the node record), the dispatch-time recording reaches no landing, so the section's remedy cannot be met and the fenced worker is blocked at its fourth case.
findings.text: §3 says the value given "is recorded in the pointer's `dispatch_options`" and that `_require_brief_owner` "reads it when `crew complete` or `crew merge` is given neither flag", but the pointer §3 writes is the queued request's, and the launched pointer is composed afresh in `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` (the record literal at `dispatch.py:2873–3094`, which copies only `route_fallback` out of `dispatch_options` at `:3020`). Measured on the live crew home at `803b7fcd1d`: all 9 not-yet-launched pointers cite `dispatch_options`, while all 27 launched pointers (`working`, `complete`, `blocked`) have no `dispatch_options` key, and none carries a `plan_link` and none carries an `unplanned_reason` key. Promotion reads `read_pointer(run_id)` (`promotion.py:1125`, `:2016`), so at landing the recorded link is absent and §3's case 4 — "its landing discharge passes with no landing flag" — cannot pass as delivered; the worker is fenced out of `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`, where the carrier would have to be added

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited location resolves against `803b7fcd1d`: `crew_dispatch` at `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:1456` with `--plan` at 1157 and `--brief` at 1159, the pair split `if pair_backend:` at 1826, the dry-run `plan_dispatch` call at 1922, `dispatch_options` assembly at 1866 and 2184, `EXECUTABLE_SECTION_ROLES` at `reckon/evidence.py:277`, `_require_brief_owner` at `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:1769`, and every listed `plan_dispatch` caller (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:687, 1047, 1177, 1233, 1670, 2009`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1713`, `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2924`).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — the eight cases each make the refusal, the recording or the landing read happen, and the six negative controls name the mutation that fails a named case (dropping the refusal, refusing one role, not reading the record, treating absence as a discharge, refusing the flagged dry run, placing the check below the pair split); case 4 is the case that would fail against today's carrier, which is why it is a finding below rather than a hole here.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate logs are placed under the run directory (durable, not a scratchpad), each starting with its revision and literal command and ending in `EXIT=`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers reach a symbol; the new test is named for what it measures, and the section states its mechanism rather than its motivating incident.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — a launched run's pointer carries no `dispatch_options`, so the value §3 records at dispatch is not present on the record `_require_brief_owner` reads at landing, and the record's composition site (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py`) is not among §3's write paths.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §3 carries one deliverable, that the plan link is asked for at dispatch and read at landing.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` declares `s3: [a-refusal-comes-before-the-work#s2]` and `s5: [#s2, #s3]`, which matches the files §3 shares (`reckon/crew/node.py` with §2) and hands on (`reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py` to §5); no missing or misdirected relationship.
